column1: # docs/walk-env-manifest.tsv — WHAT THE WALKTHROUGH HARNESS MAY PRE-SUPPLY, PER SCENARIO.
# One row per (scenario, key). The harness (nested-vsphere-lab/scripts/walk-matrix.sh) reads this
# file; scripts/check-walk-env-manifest.sh reconciles it against the documents, offline, here.
# WHY IT LIVES IN THIS REPO. The harness pre-supplies ~21 variables into the walk box before a single
# documented command runs. That list used to be hand-typed in walk_env() with nothing linking it to
# the documents it claims to walk, so it drifted in BOTH directions: a key a document requires but
# the harness never supplies makes a row die for a reason a READER would also hit (scored as a
# product bug), and a key the harness supplies that no document names makes a row green on a value no
# reader could ever have. Keeping the decision table beside the documents means the refusal fires in
# the repo whose edit caused it.
#   disposition EMIT   — the harness supplies it. The reason must say WHY a reader would have it.
#               EXEMPT — the harness does not supply it, and that is correct.
#               FORBID — the harness MUST NOT supply it. Supplying it would skip a documented
#                        command, or hand a persona a credential it does not have.
#   reason      a MECHANISM, never a state. "generated by 02-env.sh:85", not "has a default".
# THE DISPOSITION THAT MATTERS IS FORBID, and it is why this file is per-scenario rather than a flat
# list of keys. HARBOR_PASSWORD must be EMIT for scenario-2 (a tenant IS handed one — that is
# scenario-2's premise) and FORBID for scenario-1, where §8.5 fetches it. A union of the two cannot
# express that, so a gate built on one stays GREEN while the regression returns.
# THIS FIRST VERSION IS DESCRIPTIVE. Every row records what the harness does TODAY, with the reason.
# Rows whose disposition SHOULD change are marked in their reason and carry a backlog pointer —
# changing harness behaviour is a per-row validated change, not a bulk edit.
